To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Na(+)-dependent acid extrusion in insulin-secre-ting cells is regulated by the intracellular free Ca2+ concentration and that the acidification itself may be involved in the stimulus-secretion process.

1. the Na+/H+-exchange is the major mechanism for pHi-regulation in insulin-producing RIMm5F cells; 2. the Na+/Ca2+-exchange is not involved in pHi-regulation; 3. the Na+/K+-pump and the Na+/HCO3--co-transporter are not involved in pHI-regulation, and 4. the Na+/glucose-cotransporter is not involved in insulin secretion.
in insulin-secretings cells the Na+/H antiport is the primary mechanism restoring the intracellular pH after acidification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms regulating pHi and their possible involvement in the regulation of exocytosis in the insulin-secreting beta-cell.
the regulation of pHi and the role of pHi in the stimulus-secretion mechanism in RINm5 cells.
a novel mechanism for regulation of the insulin-secretory pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in RINm5 cells the regulation of [Ca2+] is independent of pHi, whereas insulin release depends on pHi.
the Na+/H+-exchanger is not involved in the insulin-secretion mechanism.
in insulin-secre-ting cells, the Na+/H(+ antiport is the most important mechanism in the regulation of intracellular acidification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of pHi is a key element in the stimulus-secretion mechanism in RINm5 cells.
in insulin-producing cells the Na+/H+-antiporter is a key regulator of pHi, and that pHi may be an essential component of the stimulus-secretion-coupling.
in RINm5 cells the Na+/H(+)-exchanger is the major mechanism regulating pHi, and the Na(+)/H(+) exchange activity is not augmented by activation of PKC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acidification of RINm5 cells by glycolysis is not the cause for insulin release.
insulin secretion is regulated in RINm5f cells by changes in intracellular pH, and not by changes in membrane potential.
the acidification of the cytoplasm, which is induced by glucose metabolism and the subsequent release of lactate and pyruvate, is an important signal for insulin exocytosis.
